title: What an agent can do with Talonic
seoTitle: Talonic MCP Server: What Your AI Agent Can Do — Talonic
description: Connect Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client to Talonic. Your agent finds documents, extracts fields, answers cited questions and runs processes.

content.text: The Talonic MCP server lets an AI agent work with the documents and data in your Talonic workspace the way you would in the web app: find a document, pull fields out of it, ask a question across everything, run a Spec, sign off a step, or set up a process. It is for anyone who wants their agent (in Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue, Cowork or their own) to do document work for them.
New here? [Connect your agent](/docs/mcp/install) in two minutes, then try the [contract question recipe](/docs/mcp/recipes/answer-a-contract-question).

items: **Find.** Locate documents by name or keyword, filter them by extracted values ("invoices over 10,000 EUR"), and find which field holds a concept. [Find tools](/docs/mcp/tools).

**Read and extract.** Turn any PDF, scan, image, DOCX or email into JSON that matches the fields you ask for, with a confidence score per field and the page and passage each value came from. Or get the full text.
**Ask.** Ask a question in plain words and get an answer with citations to the documents it rests on, checked before it is returned.
**Run.** Run one of your workspace's Specs over a set of documents and read back one clean row per document.
**Review and decide.** Sign off or send back items waiting for you, and take on checks or decisions your workspace hands to an outside agent.
**Build and automate.** Describe a process in your own words (what comes in, what is checked, who signs, what goes out), test it on real documents, publish it, and watch its runs.
**Connect and organise.** Connect a source such as a drive or mailbox, import from it, tag, move and group documents, and keep collections and saved filters.
**Author Specs and curate data.** Create, check, test and publish a Spec; review flagged values and cases; keep data products and policies current.
**Look after the workspace.** Keep each company's documents apart, check credits, pricing and usage, manage the team, retention and legal holds.

content.text: Your agent calls Talonic tools; Talonic does the reading and checking and returns structured results. Every call runs as you: it sees only your workspace and can do only what your role allows, exactly like the web app. Writes that send mail, call other systems or can't be undone say so in their description, and the agent is told to call them only when you ask.

items: **40 tools** are listed in every session.
**37 process tools** are listed when your role can see processes in the workspace.

**244 more tools** cover the rest of the workspace (Spec authoring, sources, Spec runs and ingest, organising documents, review and cases, data products, team and records administration, your thread, and app workflows). Each set is listed when your role can use that part of the workspace; [Tools by task](/docs/mcp/tools) lists them all.
Apps you have enabled (for example Contracts or Accounts Payable) add their own tools to sessions that can use them; see [Apps](https://talonic.com/docs/apps).
**Hosted** at `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`. Sign in with your Talonic account; no key to copy. Best for Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code.
**Local** with `npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest` and an API key. Best for desktop and IDE clients that start the server on your machine and can read local files.

content.text: Once connected, ask your agent: "What documents do I have in Talonic about invoices?" It calls [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) and lists them. Then: "Extract the vendor, total and due date from the first one." It calls [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract) and returns JSON with a confidence score for each field.

items: [Connect your client](/docs/mcp/install)
[Tools by task](/docs/mcp/tools)
[Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files)
[Recipe: set up a workspace end to end](/docs/mcp/recipes/set-up-a-workspace)

faq.question: Which AI clients work with the Talonic MCP server?
faq.answer: Any client that speaks the Model Context Protocol. Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue and Cowork have step-by-step instructions on the Connect page.

faq.question: Can the agent see other people's documents?
faq.answer: No. Every call runs with your credential and your workspace role, so the agent sees and changes exactly what you could in the web app, and nothing else.

faq.question: Does using the MCP server cost extra?
faq.answer: No. Tool calls use the same credits as the web app and the API. Reading, listing and searching are free; extracting, asking and running Specs use credits. Each tool page says what it costs.

title: Why connect your agent to Talonic
seoTitle: Why Connect Your AI Agent to Talonic Over MCP — Talonic
description: Reading documents inside a chat gives you text. Connecting Talonic gives your agent checked fields, cited answers, your saved Specs and processes it can run.

content.text: An agent can read a PDF you paste into a chat. What it can't do on its own is give you the same fields every time, show where each value came from, remember the thousand documents you processed last quarter, or start the approval your team runs on every invoice. Connecting Talonic adds those.

items: **Same fields, every time.** You say which fields you want once (or save them); every document comes back in that shape, with a confidence score per field.
**Evidence.** Each value links to the page and passage it came from, and answers cite the documents they rest on, so you can check before you act.
**Your whole workspace.** Questions run across every document you have added, not only the one in the chat.
**Your rules.** The agent runs the Specs and processes your team already set up, with the same permissions and sign-offs as the web app.
**Large files.** Files too big for a chat go through an upload link instead.

content.text: Start with [Connect your agent](/docs/mcp/install), or see [what an agent can do](/docs/mcp).

title: Get an API key
seoTitle: Get a Talonic API Key for the MCP Server — Talonic Docs
description: Create a Talonic API key for local MCP installs and header-based clients. Hosted connectors in Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code sign you in without a key.

content.text: A local install (`npx @talonic/mcp`) and clients that send their own headers need an API key. Hosted connectors in Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code sign you in with your Talonic account instead, so you can skip this page for those.

items: Sign in at [app.talonic.com](https://app.talonic.com).
Open **Settings → API Keys** and choose **Create key**.
Copy the key. It starts with `tlnc_` and is shown once.
Put it in your client's config as `TALONIC_API_KEY` (local) or an `Authorization: Bearer` header (hosted). [Connect your agent](/docs/mcp/install) has the snippets.

content.text: A key acts as the person who created it, in one workspace, and never with more rights than that person's role. Create a separate key per workspace and per machine so you can revoke one without breaking the others.
Keep keys out of source control and screenshots. If a key leaks, revoke it under **Settings → API Keys** and create a new one.

faq.question: Do I need an API key to use Talonic in Claude.ai or ChatGPT?
faq.answer: No. Hosted connectors sign you in with your Talonic account and keep the access token for you. You only need a key for a local install or a client that sends its own headers.

title: Connect your agent
seoTitle: Connect Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor to Talonic MCP — Talonic
description: Connect Talonic to Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue or Cowork: hosted with sign-in, or local with npx and an API key.

content.text: Connect Talonic to your AI client and your agent can work with your workspace. Pick your client below; most take under two minutes.

items: **Hosted** (`https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`): nothing to install, always the latest version, and you sign in with your Talonic account (OAuth). Files reach Talonic by URL, by document id or through an [upload link](/docs/mcp/files).

**Local** (`npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest`, Node.js 18 or later): needs an [API key](/docs/mcp/api-key). The agent can pass files on your machine by path. Pin an exact version (for example `@talonic/mcp@0.1.100`) for repeatable setups.

content.text: Both list the same tools and work on the same workspace. Signing in grants `extract:write`, `documents:read`, `schemas:read` and `apps:decide`; you can revoke access by removing the connector or the key.
Add Talonic once as a connector; it then works in Claude.ai and the Claude Desktop app.

items: Open **Settings → Connectors** in [claude.ai](https://claude.ai/settings/connectors) or Claude Desktop and choose **Add custom connector**.
Enter the URL `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`. No headers, no key.
Choose **Connect**, sign in to Talonic and approve access. If you belong to several workspaces, pick one.
Start a new conversation. The Talonic tools are available.

content.text: To run the server on your own machine instead (so the agent can read local files by path), add the local config to `claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`, Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\`) and quit and reopen Claude Desktop:

items: In ChatGPT, open **Settings → Apps**.
Find **Talonic** and choose **Connect**.
Sign in to Talonic and approve access.
In a new chat, ask for Talonic by name the first time ("Use Talonic to find my latest invoice").

content.text: ChatGPT lists every tool except the two generic data-query tools; ask questions with [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask) there. Results show as cards in the chat.
Hosted, signed in with your Talonic account:

content.code:
claude mcp add --transport http talonic https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp
# then run /mcp inside Claude Code and choose Authenticate
claude mcp add talonic --env TALONIC_API_KEY=tlnc_your_key_here -- npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest

content.text: Open **Cursor Settings → MCP → Add new MCP server**, or edit `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Use the local config to let the agent read files in your project by path:
Save and reload the window. The `talonic` entry turns green and lists its tools.
In VS Code, open the Cline panel → **MCP Servers → Configure** and add one of these, then restart the panel:
Cline can auto-approve tools. Approving the read-only ones (search, look-ups, listings) lets it explore without asking; keep writes on manual approval.
Edit `~/.continue/config.json` (shared by VS Code and JetBrains) and add an entry to `mcpServers`, then reload the IDE window:
Open **Settings → MCP Servers → Add**, paste one of these and restart Cowork:
Cowork shows your saved schemas under resources (`talonic://schemas`), so you can pick one before extracting.

Point a client that supports remote servers at `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp` (it will start a Talonic sign-in, or send `Authorization: Bearer tlnc_…`), or have it start `npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest` with `TALONIC_API_KEY` set. [Configuration](/docs/mcp/configuration) lists every setting.

Ask your agent: "List my Talonic schemas." It calls [`talonic_list_schemas`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-schemas), which is free and changes nothing. A list (or an empty list in a new workspace) means you are connected. An authentication error means the key or sign-in is wrong; see [Troubleshooting](/docs/mcp/troubleshooting).

faq.question: Should I use the hosted server or the local one?
faq.answer: Use hosted for Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code: you sign in and there is nothing to install. Use local in desktop and IDE clients when you want the agent to pass files from your machine by path.

faq.question: Do the hosted and local servers offer the same tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The only difference is that a local install can read files on your machine by path; hosted sessions use a URL, a document id or an upload link.

faq.question: How do I disconnect?
faq.answer: Remove the connector in your client, or revoke the API key under Settings → API Keys in the Talonic web app.

title: talonic_create_app
seoTitle: talonic_create_app — Create app | Talonic MCP Tool
description: Create a new app. It starts disabled with no versions; the slug can no longer change once a version is published. Part of the Talonic MCP tools for building…

content.text: Create a new app. It starts disabled with no versions; the slug can no longer change once a version is published. Listed only when the credential can read the workspace's apps. The platform checks the caller's role, per-app access and key scopes on every call.

items: USE WHEN: the user asks to set up a new app. ARGS: slug (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, 3-64 chars), display_name, mode, optional one-sentence description.

Modes: rules (decides from written rules), assisted (rules with people confirming), external (an outside agent decides through the decision-task tools), autonomous (finds candidate rules in the app's data).
RETURNS: the manifest; use its `id` (UUID) with every other app tool.

FLOW: talonic_create_app -> talonic_save_app_draft -> talonic_interpret_app_rules -> talonic_publish_app -> talonic_run_app (dry_run first) -> talonic_get_app_run / talonic_get_run_verdicts -> talonic_save_app_acceptance + talonic_check_app_acceptance -> talonic_enable_app.

params.name: slug
params.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3-64 chars.

faq.question: When is this tool listed?
faq.answer: When the credential can read the workspace's apps. The platform checks the caller's role, per-app access and key scopes on every call.

title: Documents, extractions, jobs and schemas
seoTitle: Manage Documents, Extractions, Jobs and Schemas via MCP
description: MCP tools to list, re-extract and delete Talonic documents, read and correct extracted values, run and cancel jobs over many documents, and edit saved schemas.

content.text: These tools cover the day-to-day housekeeping of a workspace: listing documents, reading a document again, correcting values, running one saved schema over many documents as a job, and changing or removing saved schemas. Every call runs as the person behind the connection: a document that person cannot see answers 404, exactly like a missing one.

The tools are listed when the connection can read the workspace's documents; changes need the `write` scope. `talonic_delete_document` and `talonic_delete_schema` cannot be undone, and `talonic_update_schema` with a new field list removes every field you do not send again. Agents confirm with the user before calling them. Re-extracting a document and creating a job consume credits and are not deduplicated: after a timeout, check the first call's result before calling again.
List documents, newest first, one page at a time. Returns `data[]` (id, filename, pages, status, source, field count, created_at) and `pagination { total, limit, has_more, next_cursor }`.

params.name: status
params.description: Only documents with this status, e.g. `error`.

params.name: source_type
params.description: Only documents from this kind of source.

params.name: parent_id
params.description: Only documents unpacked from this one (email attachments, archive members).

params.name: relation
params.description: Only nested documents of this kind.

params.name: text_degraded
params.description: `true`: only documents whose text could not be read verbatim.

params.name: order
params.description: By creation time. Default desc (newest first).

params.name: after
params.description: Only items created after this time.

params.name: before
params.description: Only items created before this time.

content.text: Read an existing document again and capture its values afresh, without uploading it again. Consumes credits like a new extraction. Answers at once with `status: processing`; poll `talonic_get_document` until it is `completed`.
Delete one document with its captured values. Cannot be undone. Documents only shared with the user are read-only and answer 404. Returns `{ deleted: true, id }`.
List extractions, one per document with captured values, newest first. An extraction's id is its document's id.

params.name: order
params.description: By creation time. Default desc (newest first).

params.name: after
params.description: Only items created after this time.

params.name: before
params.description: Only items created before this time.

content.text: One extraction in full: every field with its value, type and confidence.
One extraction's values as a flat field → value map, or as a one-row CSV (`{ format: 'csv', csv }`).

Correct captured values. Each correction is kept as a new version of the value, attributed to the connection. A value a reviewer confirmed, or one waiting for approval, is not overwritten: it is reported in `cells_skipped`. Returns the extraction with `cells_written` and `cells_skipped`.

params.name: values
params.description: `{ <field_name>: corrected value }` for the fields to change.

content.text: List jobs (one saved schema run over a set of documents), newest first.

params.name: order
params.description: By creation time. Default desc (newest first).

params.name: after
params.description: Only items created after this time.

params.name: before
params.description: Only items created before this time.

content.text: One job's status, schema, document count, timestamps and error. Poll it after `talonic_create_job`.
A job's result rows: one per document with its values, confidence and validation flags. Readable while the job still runs.

Run a saved schema over many documents and collect one row of values per document. Consumes credits per document. Name the documents, or pass `all_documents: true` for every completed document of the workspace. Returns the job id; poll `talonic_get_job`.

params.name: name
params.description: A name for the job, up to 200 characters.

content.text: Cancel a pending or running job; rows already produced stay. Safe to retry: a job that already ended answers 409 and is left as it is.

Rename a saved schema, change its description, or replace its field list. A new `definition` or `fields` list replaces every field, so read the schema first with `talonic_get_schema` and send the whole list. A schema managed by a Spec answers 409; change the Spec in the app instead.

params.name: definition
params.description: The full field list as JSON Schema: `{ properties, required }`.

params.name: fields
params.description: The full field list as rows: `field_name`, `display_name`, `data_type`, `description`, `is_required`.

content.text: Delete a saved schema. Cannot be undone; documents already extracted with it keep their values. A schema managed by a Spec answers 409.

seoTitle: talonic_list_events — Read the Talonic Workspace Event Feed
description: MCP tool that reads your Talonic workspace's event feed (extractions, run results, review verdicts, deliveries) and resumes from a saved cursor later.

content.text: **`talonic_list_events`** reads what happened in the workspace: documents extracted, runs completed or failed, review verdicts, delivery outcomes. These are the same events your webhooks receive, so an agent or a scheduled job can catch up on anything a webhook missed, or answer “what failed since this morning?”.
Listed when the connection can read the workspace. Only events about documents the connected person may see are returned.

Two ways to page. Without `after` you get the newest events first, paged with `limit` and `offset`. With `after` set to an event id or a saved `next_cursor`, you get strictly newer events, oldest first: process them in order, save the returned `next_cursor`, and pass it as `after` next time. `next_cursor` is `null` only at the end of the feed.

params.name: after
params.description: Resume point: a saved `next_cursor` or an event id. Returns newer events, oldest first.

params.name: since
params.description: Only events created at or after this ISO-8601 time.

params.name: offset
params.description: Events to skip on the newest-first listing.

title: Workspace metrics
seoTitle: talonic_aggregate — Workspace Metrics in One MCP Call
description: MCP tools that answer monitoring questions about a Talonic workspace in one call: documents received or failed, app verdicts, deliveries and cost per document.

content.text: Ask for several numbers about the workspace in one request: how many documents arrived or failed in the last 12 hours, how many lack a value, verdicts by state, median cost per document. Only numbers come back, never document content, and only documents the connected person may see are counted.
Listed when the workspace offers metrics to the connection. One metrics request per workspace runs at a time; a second one answers 429 and should be retried after a few seconds.

What can be counted: every dataset with its fields, which fields can be grouped and filtered with which operators, the measures, the limits (window length, queries per request) and whether this workspace may see cost fields. Free; call it before the first metrics request.

Computes several named numbers (20 by default) over a half-open window `[from, to)` of at most 31 days by default; the catalog states the limits that apply. Each query picks a dataset and a measure (`count`, `count_distinct`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `median`, `p1`-`p99`), optional filters and up to three group-by fields or `hour` / `day`. A count over nothing is `0`; an average or percentile over nothing is `null`. Cost fields are in US dollars.

params.name: from
params.description: Window start, inclusive, ISO-8601 with an offset (`2026-11-05T12:00:00Z`).

params.name: to
params.description: Window end, exclusive, with an offset.

params.name: queries
params.description: Each `{ id, dataset, measure, of?, where?, group_by? }`; `id` is lowercase letters, digits and underscores and keys the result.

content.text: Errors: `400 invalid_aggregate` names the allowed datasets, fields or measures; `403 cost_not_visible` when the workspace may not see costs; `422 aggregate_timeout` names the dataset to narrow.

title: Workspace administration
seoTitle: Workspace Admin Tools — API Keys, Webhooks, Credits
description: MCP tools for Talonic workspace admins: list, create and revoke API keys, manage webhooks and their event types, read the account and get a buy-credits link.

content.text: Manage the workspace from an agent: API keys, webhooks, the account snapshot and the link where a person buys credits. Each tool calls the same Talonic API your dashboard uses, with your credential.

These tools are meant for workspace admins. Talonic checks every call against the person behind the credential, exactly as in the app: an owner manages every key, anyone else only their own, and a new key can never carry more access than the credential that creates it. A new key's secret is shown once, in the create response; store it straight away.
The workspace's API keys with name, scopes, masked prefix, active state, last use and expiry. Never returns a secret.
Creates a key and returns its secret once in `key`. Scopes can only be a subset of the calling credential's own; `billing`, `usage` and `records_write` are granted only by an owner in the app.

params.name: scopes
params.description: Subset of extract, read, write, operations, billing, delivery, usage, records_write. Default: the calling credential's scopes.

params.name: expires_at
params.description: ISO-8601 time in the future when the key stops working.

content.text: Revokes a key at once; it cannot be turned back on. Marked destructive, so clients ask before running it.
Plan (`tier`), status, credit balance in EUR, daily request limits and today's usage against them.
Every webhook with its URL, event types, active state and optional source. Signing secrets are never returned.
Sends the chosen events to your URL as signed POST requests (`X-Talonic-Signature: sha256=<hex>` over the raw body when a secret is set).
Changes only the fields you send. `is_active: false` pauses deliveries without deleting the webhook.
Deletes a webhook for good. Marked destructive. To stop deliveries for a while, pause it instead.
The event types a webhook can subscribe to, each with a description. A past webhook call is not re-sent; a receiver that missed events reads them with `talonic_list_events` from its saved cursor.

A link where a person buys credits. The tool never buys anything: a human opens the link and completes the payment, and credits arrive seconds later. Workspaces billed through a marketplace get the marketplace page.

title: Compliance
seoTitle: Compliance MCP Tools — Check Documents Against Rules

content.text: Check workspace documents against the regulations, policies and standards the workspace holds as frameworks. Each rule of a framework that is ON gets a verdict per document (or per document set): pass, fail, unclear or not applicable, with the reason and the quote it rests on.

The usual loop: **`talonic_compliance_issues`** lists what fails, **`talonic_compliance_get_document_evaluation`** shows the evidence for one document, and the allowed correction follows: re-evaluate after the document changed, take a document off the list, switch a framework OFF, or narrow the rules a document set is judged against. A workspace that makes its compliance decisions with its own agent works them through the task tools (claim, heartbeat, release, submit).

These tools are listed only when the Compliance app is available to the connection. Every call is checked against the role and permissions of the person behind the connection, exactly as in the web app.
