title: Tools by task
seoTitle: Talonic MCP Tools by Task: Find, Extract, Ask, Run — Talonic
description: Every Talonic MCP tool grouped by the job: find documents, extract fields, ask cited questions, run Specs, review, build and run processes, check credits.

content.text: Pick the job, then the tool. Your agent reads the same descriptions and usually chooses well on its own; this page is for you to see what is possible and to steer it.

Rule of thumb: a question about what documents say goes to [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask); a named file goes through [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) first; fields from one document come from [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract).

Start here when the user names a document, a value or a concept. [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) turns a file name or keyword into a `document_id`; [`talonic_filter`](/docs/mcp/tools/filter) finds documents by an extracted value; [`talonic_find_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/find-data) finds which field holds a concept.

items: [`talonic_get_document`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-document): Fetch a single document's metadata and processing status from the workspace.
[`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search): Find documents, fields, schemas, or sources in the workspace.
[`talonic_filter`](/docs/mcp/tools/filter): Find documents by their extracted field VALUES using composable conditions (e.g. 'invoices where total > 1000').

[`talonic_list_fields`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-fields): List the fields your workspace's documents carry (vendor name, invoice total, notice period …), each with a stable id, how established it is (maturity), data type, synonyms and how often it occurs.

[`talonic_get_field`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-field): Describe one field: what it means, its synonyms and other names, maturity, where it occurs (document and occurrence counts, first and last seen, which document types), its values (top values with counts, distinct count, examples), which schemas use it, and the fields merged into it (superseded_by).

[`talonic_field_values`](/docs/mcp/tools/field-values): Read a field's CURRENT VALUES across documents, with evidence: one row per value, with the document id, filename and type, the value, its confidence, the label it appeared under in the document, the exact source text, and how the label was matched to this field (`resolved_by`).

[`talonic_find_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/find-data): Find where the data behind a concept lives before querying anything: turns a phrase ('payment volume per transaction', 'counterparty', 'Vertragslaufzeit') into the fields, values, documents and text passages that carry it, matching what it means as well as its words, even when the field has a different name.

content.text: Get fields as JSON with [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract), or the full text with [`talonic_to_markdown`](/docs/mcp/tools/to-markdown). Save field sets you reuse; hand the user an upload link when a file can't be passed directly ([Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files)).

items: [`talonic_list_schemas`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-schemas): List the saved schemas in the workspace as compact summaries (id, short_id, name, description, version, field_count).
[`talonic_get_schema`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-schema): Get one saved schema with its full field definition (field names, types, descriptions).
[`talonic_save_schema`](/docs/mcp/tools/save-schema): Save a reusable schema to the workspace for use across future extractions.
[`talonic_to_markdown`](/docs/mcp/tools/to-markdown): Get the full text of a document as markdown, including scanned pages.
[`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract): Extract structured, schema-validated JSON from a document: PDF, scan, image, DOCX, email, or photo.
[`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload): Get a browser upload link the user opens to add a file to their workspace.

content.text: For any question about what the documents say (totals, duplicates, comparisons, a clause), call [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask) first: one call returns a cited, checked answer.

items: [`talonic_list_agent_tools`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-agent-tools): List Talonic's data tools: read-only look-ups and queries over the workspace (find_data, describe_data, query_data for a read-only SQL query over the extracted data, get_document_markdown, workspace_overview, …), each with its input schema and whether THIS credential may call it.

[`talonic_invoke_agent_tool`](/docs/mcp/tools/invoke-agent-tool): Run ONE named data tool directly and get its exact output (e.g. `query_data` for a read-only SQL SELECT over the extracted data, `describe_data` for the queryable field list, `get_document_markdown` to read a document's text).
[`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask): Ask a natural-language question over the workspace's documents and get a cited, verified answer (markdown).
[`talonic_get_answer`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-answer): Poll an ask started by talonic_ask that was still processing when the wait ended.

content.text: Connect sources and bring documents in
Connect a drive, mailbox or other system with a sign-in link the user opens, browse it, import from it and set how often it syncs. Then follow what is being read, and tune how new files are taken in.

items: [`talonic_integrations_connectors`](/docs/mcp/tools/integrations-connectors): What the workspace can connect: per connector its slug, name, kind (source or destination), method (authorize = a browser sign-in this server can start; credentials = keys or passwords, entered by a person in the Talonic web app or sent to the REST API, never through this conversation), personal (one person's own account) and available (false = not offered on this deployment).
[`talonic_integrations_connect`](/docs/mcp/tools/integrations-connect): Start connecting an account through a browser sign-in.

[`talonic_integrations_connect_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/integrations-connect-status): Where a browser connect started by talonic_integrations_connect stands: status pending (the user has not finished yet), connected, failed (with error code and message), expired or cancelled.

[`talonic_sources_connections`](/docs/mcp/tools/sources-connections): Every connected source of the workspace with its type, name, sync state, `restricted` (visible only to some people) and `connected_by`.

[`talonic_sources_browse`](/docs/mcp/tools/sources-browse): List the folders and files inside a connected source, one level and page at a time: pass `folder_id` to open a folder, `page_token` from the previous answer for the next page, `q` to search by name.
[`talonic_sources_import`](/docs/mcp/tools/sources-import): Bring chosen files from a connected source into Talonic as documents: `file_ids` from talonic_sources_browse, optional `tags`.
[`talonic_sources_imports`](/docs/mcp/tools/sources-imports): Recent imports from one connected source: their state and what each brought in.

[`talonic_sources_sync_now`](/docs/mcp/tools/sources-sync-now): Check a connected source for new and changed files now instead of waiting for its schedule (answers 202 at once; the sync runs in the background).
[`talonic_sources_sync_settings`](/docs/mcp/tools/sources-sync-settings): Read, or change, how a connected source stays in sync.
[`talonic_ingest_queue_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/ingest-queue-status): How many of the workspace's documents are in each processing state (queued, extracting, completed, error, …).
[`talonic_ingest_duplicates`](/docs/mcp/tools/ingest-duplicates): Groups of identical files in the workspace and how many documents carry a content fingerprint.

[`talonic_ingest_skipped_duplicates`](/docs/mcp/tools/ingest-skipped-duplicates): Uploads that were not processed because an identical document already existed, newest first (up to 1000), each naming the existing document.
[`talonic_ingest_process_duplicate`](/docs/mcp/tools/ingest-process-duplicate): Create a new document for an upload that was skipped as a duplicate.

[`talonic_ingest_settings`](/docs/mcp/tools/ingest-settings): Which optional steps run when documents arrive in this workspace, each on by default: `classification` (document types), `triage` (sensitivity tags), `grounding_gate` (checking low-confidence values against the page), `entity_linking` (links between documents), `delivery` (the `document.extracted` notification to webhooks and destinations) and `registry_binding` (matching values to the workspace's fields).
[`talonic_ingest_update_settings`](/docs/mcp/tools/ingest-update-settings): Turn optional ingest steps on or off; only the steps given change.

content.text: Tag, move, rename and delete documents, group them into collections, keep saved filters, and confirm or correct the document type Talonic suggests.

items: [`talonic_documents_tags`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-tags): Every distinct tag on documents the key's person can see.
[`talonic_documents_system_tags`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-system-tags): Distinct grouping tags Talonic set on visible documents when it unpacked them (the email or archive a document came in).
[`talonic_documents_facets`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-facets): How many visible documents have each status, document type, source and tag.
[`talonic_documents_batch_tag`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-batch-tag): Add, remove or set tags on up to 1000 documents in one call.
[`talonic_documents_set_tags`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-set-tags): Replace one document's tags with exactly the given list; an empty list clears them.

[`talonic_documents_import_batch_ids`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-import-batch-ids): Set the source batch id of existing documents from a list or a CSV, e.g. to group documents by the delivery or job they came in.

[`talonic_documents_display_name_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-display-name-rule): The workspace's rule for showing documents under a readable name instead of their raw filename: `mode` `off`, `default` (tidy the filename) or `lua` (a script), the script if any, and a sample of current filename → name pairs.

[`talonic_documents_set_display_name_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-set-display-name-rule): Set how documents get their readable name: `off` (show filenames; clears the readable names already stored), `default` (tidy the filename) or `lua` with a `script`.

[`talonic_documents_preview_display_name_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-preview-display-name-rule): Run a candidate rule script over a random sample of the workspace's real filenames and show the names it would give, without saving anything.

[`talonic_documents_generate_display_name_script`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-generate-display-name-script): Draft a rule script from a plain-language instruction, e.g. "drop the number in front of the name and the date at the end", using the workspace's own filenames as examples.

[`talonic_documents_display_name_coverage`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-display-name-coverage): How many documents carry a readable name, how many differ from their filename, and a sample of documents still shown under their raw filename.

[`talonic_documents_backfill_display_names`](/docs/mcp/tools/documents-backfill-display-names): Apply the current readable-name rule to every existing document, overwriting the readable names they have.
[`talonic_collections_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-list): The workspace's collections.
[`talonic_collections_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-create): Create a collection (or, with kind `account`, an account).

[`talonic_collections_preview`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-preview): A sample of the documents the collection holds under its current rules and hand-added documents, limited to what the key's person can see.
[`talonic_collections_update`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-update): Rename or describe a collection, or change its kind or aliases.
[`talonic_collections_delete`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-delete): Delete a collection with its rules, hand-added documents and assignments.
[`talonic_collections_rules`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-rules): The rules that fill a collection: each names a `rule_type` and a `rule_value`.

[`talonic_collections_add_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-add-rule): Add a rule: every document of a source (`source_connection`, value = the source id), a document type (`document_type`, value = the type id) or a case (`case`, value = the case id) joins the collection, including documents that arrive later.
[`talonic_collections_remove_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-remove-rule): Remove one rule; the documents it brought in leave the collection unless another rule or a hand-add keeps them.
[`talonic_collections_documents`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-documents): The documents added to a collection by hand (not those its rules bring in), limited to what the key's person can see.
[`talonic_collections_add_documents`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-add-documents): Add documents to a collection by hand.
[`talonic_collections_remove_document`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-remove-document): Take one hand-added document out of a collection.
[`talonic_collections_assignments`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-assignments): The people and groups a collection is assigned to, each with its mode (`enforced` or `default`).
[`talonic_collections_assign`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-assign): Assign a collection to a person (`user`) or a `group`.
[`talonic_collections_unassign`](/docs/mcp/tools/collections-unassign): Remove one assignment.
[`talonic_saved_filters_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/saved-filters-list): The workspace's saved filter presets, newest first: name, conditions, search text, sort and source.
[`talonic_saved_filters_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/saved-filters-create): Save a filter preset for the key's person, so it appears in their filter picker in the web app.
[`talonic_saved_filters_delete`](/docs/mcp/tools/saved-filters-delete): Delete one of the key's person's own saved filters (404 for anyone else's).
[`talonic_document_types_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-list): The workspace's document types with how many documents each has, most used first.
[`talonic_document_types_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-create): Create a document type for the workspace.
[`talonic_document_types_update`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-update): Rename a document type or change its description.

[`talonic_document_types_pending`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-pending): Document types proposed while new documents were sorted, waiting for a decision, with suggestions: create as is, merge similar proposals together, or merge into a close existing type.
[`talonic_document_types_resolve_pending`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-resolve-pending): Settle one proposal: `create` makes the proposed type, `merge` folds it into `merge_into_type_id`.
[`talonic_document_types_resolve_pending_batch`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-resolve-pending-batch): Settle up to 200 proposals in one call, each with `create` or `merge`.
[`talonic_document_types_merge_pending`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-merge-pending): Merge several proposals into one new type named `chosen_name`; their documents move to it.

[`talonic_document_types_auto_resolve`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-auto-resolve): Settle every waiting proposal automatically: each is matched to Talonic's standard type list and merged where a matching type exists; the rest are created.
[`talonic_document_types_dismiss_pending`](/docs/mcp/tools/document-types-dismiss-pending): Dismiss one proposal without creating a type.

content.text: A Spec is a saved set of fields and checks your team set up in Talonic. Run it over documents to get one clean row per document.

items: [`talonic_list_specs`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-specs): List the workspace's Specs.

[`talonic_get_spec`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-spec): Get one Spec's structure: identity and version state, the schema its output rows follow, `nodes[]` (the steps as the user set them up, in editing order), `phases[]` (the same steps in the order a run carries them out; one check can appear more than once, so the two lists can differ), and `fields[]` (Spec field ↔ schema field).
[`talonic_run_spec`](/docs/mcp/tools/run-spec): Run one of the workspace's Specs over documents, in one call, and get one structured row per document.
[`talonic_get_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-run): Poll a Spec run started by talonic_run_spec: normalised status plus progress per document and, for run_kind 'pipeline', per step.

[`talonic_get_run_results`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-run-results): Read a Spec run's structured rows — one row per document with the Spec's fields as clean values (values held for review come back null), plus the column definitions.
[`talonic_pipeline_add_documents`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-add-documents): Attach workspace documents to a Spec run.
[`talonic_pipeline_documents`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-documents): The documents of a Spec run with their processing state, paged and filterable like the run grid in the web app.
[`talonic_pipeline_runs`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-runs): The submission groups (`run_id`) that fed documents into a Spec run, newest first, paged, with how many documents each holds.
[`talonic_pipeline_start`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-start): Start (or resume) processing of the run's idle documents, e.g. after talonic_pipeline_add_documents.
[`talonic_pipeline_retry_errored`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-retry-errored): Process again only the run's documents that failed; documents that finished are untouched.

[`talonic_pipeline_retriage`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-retriage): Rebuild a finished run's review queue from its stored check results and route the items again, optionally under a new `review_config`.

[`talonic_pipeline_field_states`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-field-states): The state of every field of one document in a Spec run: value, confidence, whether it is flagged, waits for review, or was changed by a person.
[`talonic_pipeline_cell_history`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-cell-history): Every value each cell of the run held, who or what set it, and when.

[`talonic_pipeline_assembly_groups`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-assembly-groups): For a Spec that assembles several documents into one record (e.g. an order with its invoices): every group with its row, its base document and the documents bucketed into it.

[`talonic_pipeline_needs_anchor`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-needs-anchor): Groups of an assembling Spec run that could not settle on one base document, each with the candidate documents to choose from.
[`talonic_pipeline_resolve_anchor`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-resolve-anchor): Settle one group by choosing its base document; the group is assembled again around it.
[`talonic_pipeline_rerun_assembly`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-rerun-assembly): Assemble every group of the run again from its current documents.
[`talonic_pipeline_rule_holds`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-rule-holds): The business-rule holds that stop this Spec's runs, each with the runs it holds and the one-run overrides already given.
[`talonic_pipeline_override_hold`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-override-hold): Let exactly one held run proceed despite a business-rule hold, with a reason kept on the audit trail.

[`talonic_pipeline_reconciliation_cases`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-reconciliation-cases): The reconciliation cases this Spec's business rules raised (a mismatch between documents to look into), with their state.

[`talonic_pipeline_export_reconciliation_cases`](/docs/mcp/tools/pipeline-export-reconciliation-cases): The full audit export of a Spec's reconciliation cases: the values each case saw, its evidence, its history and the holds it caused.

content.text: Create a Spec from a document, an export or a schema, edit it under its revision, check and test it on real documents, then publish it or roll back to an earlier version.

items: [`talonic_spec_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/spec-create): Create a Spec (a saved extraction pipeline: the fields to capture and the steps that produce them).
[`talonic_spec_edit`](/docs/mcp/tools/spec-edit): Read or change a Spec's draft.
[`talonic_spec_check`](/docs/mcp/tools/spec-check): Check a Spec without saving anything: the draft, or `doc` before you save it.
[`talonic_spec_test`](/docs/mcp/tools/spec-test): Test the draft on sample documents: a preview run that is never delivered to the workspace's destinations.
[`talonic_spec_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/spec-publish): Publish the draft as the next version: new runs use it from now on.
[`talonic_spec_rollback`](/docs/mcp/tools/spec-rollback): Go back to an earlier published version: its document is published again as a NEW version (history is kept).

content.text: Work that waits for a person or an outside agent: sign-offs and forms waiting for the user, checks a Spec hands to your agent, and decisions an app hands out. [Run Talonic tasks from your own agent](/docs/mcp/run-talonic-tasks) explains the claim, work, submit loop.

items: [`talonic_list_agent_tasks`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-agent-tasks): List the agent tasks waiting in this workspace: checks a Spec hands to an outside agent (your agent) instead of a person, one per document.
[`talonic_get_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-agent-task): Read one agent task: its fixed input, instructions, and the output fields it expects.
[`talonic_claim_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/claim-agent-task): Claim an available agent task so no one else works on it, or reclaim it after its lease expires.
[`talonic_heartbeat_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/heartbeat-agent-task): Extend the lease on a claimed agent task so you keep it while you work.
[`talonic_submit_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/submit-agent-task): Submit the output fields for a claimed agent task; the document then continues through its Spec.
[`talonic_list_decision_tasks`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-decision-tasks): List one External-mode app's decision tasks (runs waiting for an outside agent to decide), newest first.

[`talonic_claim_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/claim-decision-task): Claim an available decision task (or reclaim one whose lease expired) and receive the decision bundle: task metadata with the new execution_epoch, output_contract, precedents, and a package descriptor { package_kind, record_count, page_size, first_cursor, documents }.

[`talonic_read_decision_package`](/docs/mcp/tools/read-decision-package): Read one page of a claimed decision task's fixed input: the records the decision must be made from, each with the locator to cite as evidence.
[`talonic_heartbeat_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/heartbeat-decision-task): Extend the lease on a claimed decision task, never past its sla_deadline_at.
[`talonic_submit_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/submit-decision-task): Submit the decision for a claimed decision task; Talonic checks it before saving anything, then the run continues.
[`talonic_release_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/release-decision-task): Release a claimed decision task back to 'available' without deciding it; the next claim bumps the epoch.

[`talonic_fail_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/fail-decision-task): Report that the claimed decision task cannot be decided: sends it to a person for review with your reason AND applies the app's declared fallback policy (rules decide, hold for review, or fail the run).
[`talonic_process_waiting_for_me`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-waiting-for-me): Sign-offs and forms waiting for the caller (the person behind the key): per process and step, how many items wait.
[`talonic_process_sign`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-sign): Sign a sign-off step of a run for the caller: approve all waiting items, or only `items`.
[`talonic_process_send_back`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-send-back): Send items back from a sign-off step with a reason, for the caller: the opposite of talonic_process_sign.
[`talonic_review_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-list): The review queue: values held for a human decision before they count, newest first, each with its current value, confidence and why it is held.
[`talonic_review_claim`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-claim): Claim the next review items for the person behind the credential, in queue order under the filters.
[`talonic_review_claims`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-claims): Keep the listed claims alive (touch) or hand them back to the queue (release).
[`talonic_review_assign`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-assign): Claim (assign: true) or release (assign: false) one review item for the person behind the credential.

[`talonic_review_inspect`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-inspect): The evidence behind a held value: the value, its history, check results, prior decisions and the source passages it came from with their document and page.

[`talonic_review_reference_view`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-reference-view): Every field of one document in a run beside its reference value (reference table, a check's expected value, or the matched master record); status none when there is no reference.
[`talonic_review_resolve`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-resolve): Decide a held value: approve keeps it, correct or override promotes corrected_value, accept_proposal promotes a proposed correction.
[`talonic_review_propose_correction`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-propose-correction): Propose a new value for a field that is NOT in review: it re-opens for a reviewer with your proposal attached.
[`talonic_review_recommend`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-recommend): Leave a recommendation on an item the person behind the credential may not decide (a field marked complex), for a reviewer who can.
[`talonic_review_decisions`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-decisions): Who decided what: prior and final value, action and reason per field.
[`talonic_review_metrics`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-metrics): How far review of one run has come: fields that entered review, fields decided, and the approved / corrected / overridden mix.
[`talonic_review_notes`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-notes): Reviewer guidance kept for everyone reviewing a field, newest first.
[`talonic_review_add_note`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-add-note): Add guidance to a field for everyone reviewing it, written as the person behind the credential.
[`talonic_review_bulk_approve`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-bulk-approve): Approve many results waiting for approval at once, as the person behind the credential.
[`talonic_review_compare_sources`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-compare-sources): Field by field, what each source said for an approval decision, with the supporting passage, to choose the value to keep.
[`talonic_review_choose_value`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-choose-value): Record the value to keep for one field of an approval decision, from a source (source_pick) or typed (free_text).

[`talonic_review_list_benchmarks`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-list-benchmarks): Benchmark runs (comparisons against your own answers and run reviews), or with kind: checks the run-to-run comparisons and rule checks, newest first.

[`talonic_review_field_accuracy`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-field-accuracy): Expected against extracted values of one field across a benchmark's documents: where the field is right and how it goes wrong.
[`talonic_review_decide_flags`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-decide-flags): Decide values a run review flagged: accepting applies the suggested value, rejecting keeps the original.
[`talonic_review_flag_progress`](/docs/mcp/tools/review-flag-progress): Progress of a run review: how many values were checked and how many are flagged.
[`talonic_cases_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-list): The workspace's cases: documents grouped by the references they make to each other.

[`talonic_cases_get`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-get): One case: its documents, the links between them with the quoted passage for each, its name, whether it is resolved, and the documents it references but lacks.
[`talonic_cases_update`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-update): Rename a case, mark it resolved, or reopen it.
[`talonic_cases_narrate`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-narrate): The case's title and a short narrative of what happened, in a language.
[`talonic_cases_references_to_review`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-references-to-review): References that match more than one document, each with its candidate documents, waiting for a person to decide.
[`talonic_cases_resolve_reference`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-resolve-reference): Decide which document a reference points to.
[`talonic_cases_reject_reference`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-reject-reference): Reject a reference as not a real link between documents.
[`talonic_cases_missing_documents`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-missing-documents): Documents your documents reference that were never uploaded, grouped by reference.
[`talonic_cases_document_neighbors`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-document-neighbors): Documents one step from a document, with the field and value that connects them.
[`talonic_cases_list_templates`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-list-templates): Case templates: the document types a complete case of each kind holds.
[`talonic_cases_save_template`](/docs/mcp/tools/cases-save-template): Create a case template (no template_id) or change one (with template_id).

[`talonic_schema_review_queue`](/docs/mcp/tools/schema-review-queue): List the schema changes waiting for a decision (those that add, remove or retype fields in a way that can affect existing output), newest first.
[`talonic_schema_review_approve`](/docs/mcp/tools/schema-review-approve): Approve a schema change from the review queue: it becomes the live version.
[`talonic_schema_review_reject`](/docs/mcp/tools/schema-review-reject): Reject a schema change from the review queue and discard the proposed changes.
[`talonic_link_key_set`](/docs/mcp/tools/link-key-set): Make a field a link key of the workspace (documents that share its value are linked), or stop using it as one.

content.text: Data products, policies and the catalog
Keep shared data products and data policies current, browse the workspace data catalog and its rows, and decide suggested questions, mappings and links.

items: [`talonic_data_product_update_definition`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-update-definition): Replace the definition of a shared data product (the keyed dataset several runs contribute to: identity, roles, readiness rules).
[`talonic_data_product_runs`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-runs): List the runs a run-backed data product reads its rows from, with their progress (documents total, completed, failed).

[`talonic_data_product_add_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-add-run): Link one more run (a structuring run or a resolution run of the workspace) to a run-backed data product; its rows appear in the product on the next read.
[`talonic_data_product_remove_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-remove-run): Unlink a run from a data product; its rows leave the product on the next read.

[`talonic_data_product_disagreements`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-disagreements): For a product built to compare runs: every field where the runs produced different values, grouped by document, with each run's value, confidence and the decision taken so far, plus totals pending and reviewed.

[`talonic_data_product_resolve_field`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-resolve-field): Record the value to keep for one field of one document where the runs disagree, how it was chosen (`selection_method`, for example `run` or `manual`) and the candidates seen (`source_values`, one per run).

[`talonic_data_product_suggest_resolutions`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-suggest-resolutions): Read each document behind a disagreeing field and suggest the value to keep, with a confidence (0-1) and a short reason, as document_id → field_name → suggestion.

[`talonic_data_product_resolve_singles`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-resolve-singles): Decide every disagreeing field where exactly one run has a value and the others are empty, keeping that value; answers how many were decided.

[`talonic_data_product_issue_ids`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-issue-ids): Issue unique IDs into the product's rows by its ID rules, or by the `rules` you send (target_field, condition empty|always, source_field, format containing {value} and {seq:N}).
[`talonic_data_product_regenerate_ids`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-regenerate-ids): Clear every issued ID of the product and issue them again from its rules.
[`talonic_data_product_generated_ids`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-generated-ids): List every ID issued for the product's rows.
[`talonic_data_product_sequence_counters`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-sequence-counters): List the counters the product's ID rules draw from, per target field and prefix, with their current value.
[`talonic_data_product_set_sequence_counter`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-set-sequence-counter): Set a counter's high-water mark; the next ID issued is value + 1.
[`talonic_data_product_counter_ids`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-product-counter-ids): List the IDs one counter issued, per document, newest first, paged with limit and offset.
[`talonic_data_policy_check`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-policy-check): Check a data policy's latest version and prepare it to run; answers `{id, status: "compiled", rule_count}`.

[`talonic_data_policy_preview`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-policy-preview): Preview a data policy's latest version on one record set without writing anything: one sample record as the policy would leave it and how many records the set holds (`{ok, sample, total_records}`).
[`talonic_data_policy_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-policy-publish): Publish a data policy's latest checked version and make it the one runs use.
[`talonic_data_policy_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/data-policy-run): Apply a data policy's published version to a completed structuring run and start it; answers 202 with the new run.
[`talonic_catalog_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/catalog-list): List every data set shared in the workspace: its fields with their meaning, row count and when it was last updated.
[`talonic_catalog_get`](/docs/mcp/tools/catalog-get): One data set of the workspace catalog by name: fields, row count, status, last update.
[`talonic_catalog_rows`](/docs/mcp/tools/catalog-rows): Read rows of one data set, each with the documents it came from.

[`talonic_suggestion_questions`](/docs/mcp/tools/suggestion-questions): List the questions Talonic asks a person about the workspace's data (which field a column holds, whether two records are the same party, a changed format), open ones first, most important first.

[`talonic_suggestion_answer`](/docs/mcp/tools/suggestion-answer): Answer a question with one of its options (`option` is the option's `index`); the answer applies to every subject the question covers and is recorded for the caller. 409 when the question is no longer open.
[`talonic_suggestion_mappings`](/docs/mcp/tools/suggestion-mappings): List suggested fields for the columns of connected sources, with a confidence.

[`talonic_suggestion_decide_mapping`](/docs/mcp/tools/suggestion-decide-mapping): Confirm or reject a suggested mapping, or retarget it to another field (`field_registry_id`, from talonic_list_fields) or to a proposed new field (`proposed` with canonical_name).

[`talonic_suggestion_links`](/docs/mcp/tools/suggestion-links): List suggested matches between a column of one table and a column of another (one refers to the other, or they share values), with how much they overlap.
[`talonic_suggestion_decide_link`](/docs/mcp/tools/suggestion-decide-link): Confirm or reject a suggested match between tables; recorded for the caller.

content.text: Describe a process in plain words, check it, test it on real documents in a test copy, then publish it. Nothing runs for real until [`talonic_process_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-publish). Process tools are listed when your role can see processes.

items: [`talonic_process_get`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-get): One process with its draft: fields, steps (id, kind, name, settings) and the arrows between them.
[`talonic_process_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-create): Set up a new process as a DRAFT.
[`talonic_process_change`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-change): Change a process draft from an instruction in plain words: add, remove or reorder steps, change who decides, what is sent, any setting.

[`talonic_process_check`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-check): What a draft still needs before it can go live (`stillNeeded`, per step), every problem the check finds, and what publishing would change against the live version.
[`talonic_process_test_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-test-run): Run the DRAFT on real documents in a test copy: nothing is delivered, emailed or called.
[`talonic_process_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-publish): Make the draft the LIVE version.
[`talonic_process_versions`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-versions): The published versions of a process, newest first, with who published and why.
[`talonic_process_rollback`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-rollback): Make an earlier published version live again.
[`talonic_process_delete`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-delete): Delete a process.

[`talonic_process_setup`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-setup): What processes of this workspace can use: who a step can wait for (roles, groups), the connected mailboxes and whether each may send, the names of stored secrets (never values), and the shared data a look-up step can read.

[`talonic_process_mailbox_ownership`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-mailbox-ownership): Say whether a connected mailbox is one person's own (`individual`: only that person may put it on a process) or the company's (`company`: everyone who builds processes may).
[`talonic_process_address`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-address): The address other systems send items to (a webhook).
[`talonic_process_details`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-details): Rename a process, put it in a folder (`folder: null` takes it out) or replace its tags.
[`talonic_process_export`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-export): The process draft as a file another workspace can import (pass its `doc` as `draft` with a name when creating a process there).
[`talonic_process_resources`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-resources): What a published version made or uses in the workspace: schemas, deliveries, policies and the like, with the steps they belong to.

[`talonic_process_extract_pipeline`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-extract-pipeline): Move the draft's document steps (reading, checking, reviewing documents) and its fields into a new reusable pipeline that other processes can use too; one pipeline step takes their place in the draft.

[`talonic_process_try`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-try): Walk the draft with made-up values (by field id, from talonic_process_get) and sign-off choices (by step id): the steps an item would take and where it stops.
[`talonic_process_form_preview`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-form-preview): How a form step of the draft looks to the person filling it in: title, intro, button and fields with their kinds and choices.
[`talonic_process_examples`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-examples): Examples are items kept from runs that a draft is checked against with talonic_process_evaluate.

[`talonic_process_evaluate`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-evaluate): Check the draft against every kept example: how many still go the same way, and for each that would now go another way, where the ways part.
[`talonic_process_scripts`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-scripts): Per script step of the draft, the latest test (by the script's `hash`, passed or not, with results) and approval.
[`talonic_process_script_draft`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-script-draft): Write a script for a script step from what it should do, in plain words.

[`talonic_process_script_test`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-script-test): Test a script step's current script on up to 10 recent records of this process, writing nothing: before and after per field, and `ok`.
[`talonic_process_script_approve`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-script-approve): Approve the exact script that passed its test, by its `hash` from talonic_process_scripts.

[`talonic_process_group`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-group): Create, change or delete a group of people a sign-off or form step can wait for (the same groups as Team & Roles; list them with talonic_process_setup).
[`talonic_process_build_lookup_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-build-lookup-data): Build the shared data look-up steps read, from the reference data and snapshots the workspace holds.

content.text: Start a published process for one item, see where its runs stand, follow one item through every step, and retry failed steps once the cause is fixed.

items: [`talonic_process_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-list): List the workspace's processes: name, live version (null = draft only), folder, tags and number of steps.
[`talonic_process_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-run): Start a published process for one item with values by field name, e.g. {"Vendor": "Acme", "Amount": 1200}.
[`talonic_process_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-status): Where a process run stands: per step, how many items are waiting, done or failed, and each item's state.
[`talonic_process_runs`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-runs): Runs across all processes, newest first: state (running, completed, failed, stuck = open with a failed item), items done, waiting and failed.
[`talonic_process_item`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-item): One item's way through a run, step by step (status, time, note such as why it stopped or where a mail went), and its values now.
[`talonic_process_retry`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-retry): Try every failed step of a run again.

[`talonic_process_sign_off`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-sign-off): One sign-off step as the caller sees it: the brief (who signs, instructions, fields, choices), whether the caller may sign, and only then the items waiting with the values to check and the latest decisions.

[`talonic_process_retry_item`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-retry-item): Try one failed step again for one item of a run: an email or a call is sent again, an item a signer sent back goes back to its signers.

content.text: Your thread, the agent and My Data
Read and write in your Talonic thread, decide approvals, drafts and sheets waiting in it, confirm an agent turn, and see and share the data Talonic holds about you.

items: [`talonic_thread_state`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-state): Read the person's thread: the last exchange and any card waiting for their decision, plus the cursor to read later events from.
[`talonic_thread_events`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-events): Read everything written to the person's thread after a cursor, oldest first: their messages, the answers, decision cards and status rows.
[`talonic_thread_send`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-send): Send one message to the person's thread, as them, and wait up to `wait_seconds` for the answer.
[`talonic_thread_send_files`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-send-files): Hand the person's thread up to five files with an optional message.
[`talonic_thread_decide_approval`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-decide-approval): Approve or decline an action the thread is holding for the person (an approval card without a draft).

[`talonic_thread_list_drafts`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-list-drafts): List the drafts the thread prepared and is waiting for the person to approve: an email, a start of one of their processes, or sharing one of their documents.
[`talonic_thread_decide_draft`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-decide-draft): Approve or decline one prepared draft, naming the version the person saw.
[`talonic_thread_list_sheets`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-list-sheets): List the person's screens: tasks over a set of records (contracts to renew, invoices to check) the thread opened for them.

[`talonic_thread_get_sheet`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-get-sheet): Read one screen: its records as the person can read them now, the choices it offers, and what was written about each record (suggestion, reason, decision, version).
[`talonic_thread_decide_sheet`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-decide-sheet): Record, change or take back (decision null) the person's decision on one record of a screen, naming the record version they saw.
[`talonic_thread_close_sheet`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-close-sheet): Mark one of the person's screens done.
[`talonic_thread_figure`](/docs/mcp/tools/thread-figure): Check one figure the thread stated: how it was counted, the records behind it, and whether anything changed since.
[`talonic_agent_get_turn`](/docs/mcp/tools/agent-get-turn): Read one of the person's agent turns: status (awaiting_confirmation while a step waits for their decision), events and result.
[`talonic_agent_confirm_turn`](/docs/mcp/tools/agent-confirm-turn): Run (confirmed true) or decline (false) the step one of the person's turns is waiting for.
[`talonic_agent_home_page`](/docs/mcp/tools/agent-home-page): Read the person's own home page in the workspace: its HTML, when it was built, and how many builds back it can be stepped.
[`talonic_my_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/my-data): Read the person's own data: per source they connected and item they brought in, who can see it now (only_me, shared, company).
[`talonic_my_data_share`](/docs/mcp/tools/my-data-share): Share a source the person connected with named colleagues, or stop sharing it (an empty list stops it for everyone; the person keeps access).

[`talonic_my_data_share_items`](/docs/mcp/tools/my-data-share-items): Share chosen items of a source the person connected (an email with its attachments) with one colleague, or stop sharing them (without recipient_id: with everyone).
[`talonic_my_data_field_requests`](/docs/mcp/tools/my-data-field-requests): List field requests to the person (colleagues asking for their values of a field) and by the person.

[`talonic_my_data_decide_field_request`](/docs/mcp/tools/my-data-decide-field-request): Decide a field request as the person: as holder approve, deny (with text as the reason), clarify (text as the question) or stop a grant; as asker withdraw or answer (text).

content.text: See which Talonic apps the workspace has, and work in the enabled ones: Receivables, Spend Audit, Payables Desk, Workbook capture, Compliance, Money Found, Contract Check, chart reading and business objects. Other apps (for example Contracts, Accounts Payable, Document Generation or Price Baseline) add their own tools to sessions that can use them; each app's page under [Apps](https://talonic.com/docs/apps) lists them.

items: [`talonic_list_apps`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-apps): List the Talonic Apps in the user's workspace: id, slug, name, one-line description, mode and whether each is enabled.

[`talonic_ar_overview`](/docs/mcp/tools/ar-overview): The receivables cockpit: aging of open receivables, cash application and bill-ready statistics, recoverable money found on receivables, latest decisions.

[`talonic_ar_cash_application_preview`](/docs/mcp/tools/ar-cash-application-preview): Match every remittance line to the open invoices and show the result: statistics over all remittances and one page of them, exceptions first.

[`talonic_ar_cash_application_apply`](/docs/mcp/tools/ar-cash-application-apply): Record the decisions of the cash application (payments applied or exception, invoices paid / partially paid / short paid, deductions open).

[`talonic_ar_bill_ready_preview`](/docs/mcp/tools/ar-bill-ready-preview): Per load, the checks (delivered, proof of delivery present and signed, carrier cost within contract, accessorials settled, rate agreed) and the verdict auto_bill, review or not_ready.
[`talonic_ar_bill_ready_apply`](/docs/mcp/tools/ar-bill-ready-apply): Record bill_ready or review on every load.
[`talonic_ar_tmw_mapping`](/docs/mcp/tools/ar-tmw-mapping): How Trimble TMW tables map onto the receivables inputs, with the status conventions.
[`talonic_spend_audit_get`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-get): The spend audit: every vendor with its verdicts and open to-dos, the lists it was built from, display options and assumptions.
[`talonic_spend_audit_set_options`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-set-options): Set the audit's display options.
[`talonic_spend_audit_set_assumptions`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-set-assumptions): Replace the basis and assumptions text shown under the audit.
[`talonic_spend_audit_explain_todo`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-explain-todo): Close one vendor's to-do with a reason instead of a document.
[`talonic_spend_audit_reopen_todo`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-reopen-todo): Reopen a to-do that was closed with a reason.
[`talonic_spend_audit_share`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-share): PUBLISHES the audit outside the workspace: answers a new link and password; the previous link stops working.
[`talonic_spend_audit_get_share`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-get-share): The published link and its password, or nothing when the audit is not published.
[`talonic_spend_audit_unshare`](/docs/mcp/tools/spend-audit-unshare): Revoke the published link; nobody outside the workspace can open the audit any more.
[`talonic_objects_recent`](/docs/mcp/tools/objects-recent): The latest decisions recorded on business objects (invoices, loads, payments, contracts, leases, ledger rows), newest first.
[`talonic_objects_by_type`](/docs/mcp/tools/objects-by-type): Without `state`: how many objects of a type are in each state.
[`talonic_object_get`](/docs/mcp/tools/object-get): The current state of one business object and every decision recorded on it, with who and the evidence.
[`talonic_object_record_decision`](/docs/mcp/tools/object-record-decision): Record a decision on one business object; it is attributed to this connection, never to a person.
[`talonic_payables_desk_page`](/docs/mcp/tools/payables-desk-page): One page of supplier invoices with what the checks read and found on each, or ready: false with the reason.
[`talonic_payables_desk_policy`](/docs/mcp/tools/payables-desk-policy): The payment rules in force (order and approval thresholds, currency, rates), where they come from, and their version.
[`talonic_payables_desk_save_policy`](/docs/mcp/tools/payables-desk-save-policy): Save the payment rules.
[`talonic_workbook_list_structures`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-list-structures): The workspace's target structures (each made from a client's example table) with their mapping counts.
[`talonic_workbook_create_structure`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-create-structure): Create, or replace, a target structure from the example table in a captured workbook.
[`talonic_workbook_get_structure`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-get-structure): One target structure with its fields.

[`talonic_workbook_update_structure`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-update-structure): Set field defaults and aliases (only the fields named change) and, with `checks`, replace the identity checks (a total that must equal its parts).
[`talonic_workbook_list_mappings`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-list-mappings): How each row and column label maps onto the structure, who decided it, and whether a person approved it.

[`talonic_workbook_correct_mapping`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-correct-mapping): Correct one label's mapping; it counts as approved and every later workbook uses it. scope header_leaf applies the metric or ignore decision to every column header ending in the same label.
[`talonic_workbook_approve_mapping`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-approve-mapping): Approve one label's mapping as it stands.

[`talonic_workbook_get_capture`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-get-capture): What was captured from one workbook: the run, its tables with counts, its pictures with their position. run: null when never captured.
[`talonic_workbook_checks`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-checks): Totals that do not add up and similar findings; identity findings too when `structure_id` is given.
[`talonic_workbook_facts`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-facts): The workbook's facts under a target structure, each with its figure, fields and source cell.
[`talonic_workbook_project`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-project): Map the workbook's labels and write its facts under the structure, replacing the facts it held for that structure.
[`talonic_workbook_table`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-table): One captured table rebuilt as a grid with every value cell and the header, label, title, context and note cells that give it meaning.
[`talonic_workbook_cell`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-cell): Everything known about one cell: value, raw text, scale, currency, column path, row labels, notes, formula.
[`talonic_workbook_recapture`](/docs/mcp/tools/workbook-recapture): Capture the workbook again now.
[`talonic_record_set_page`](/docs/mcp/tools/record-set-page): One page of a record set with its fields and cells, the shape the web grid shows.
[`talonic_record_set_cell_provenance`](/docs/mcp/tools/record-set-cell-provenance): One cell's value, confidence, status, source and audit reference.
[`talonic_compliance_get_framework`](/docs/mcp/tools/compliance-get-framework): One framework with its reading state, ON/OFF and its rules.
[`talonic_compliance_reread_framework`](/docs/mcp/tools/compliance-reread-framework): Read the framework's rules again from its document; the rules are replaced when the reading finishes.
[`talonic_compliance_add_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/compliance-add-rule): Add a rule written by a person to a framework.
[`talonic_compliance_update_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/compliance-update-rule): Edit one rule; only the fields sent change.
[`talonic_compliance_delete_rule`](/docs/mcp/tools/compliance-delete-rule): Take one rule out of its framework.
[`talonic_money_found_catalog`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-catalog): The roles a configuration binds, their fields, and the levers with what each needs.
[`talonic_money_found_config`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-config): The configuration in force, or config: null.
[`talonic_money_found_propose_config`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-propose-config): Propose a configuration from the workspace's Specs and tables.
[`talonic_money_found_save_config`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-save-config): Confirm a configuration (validated in full; a binding to a missing source or field is dropped).

[`talonic_money_found_structure_clauses`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-structure-clauses): Read rebate steps, rates and dates out of the configured contracts' clause text and save them into the configuration.

[`talonic_money_found_cost_clauses`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-cost-clauses): Read who bears each cost from the contracts' own text and save it; an answer counts only when its quote is found. dry_run counts only.
[`talonic_money_found_delete_config`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-delete-config): Remove the configuration; the ledger without one answers again.
[`talonic_money_found_set_row_state`](/docs/mcp/tools/money-found-set-row-state): Record open, in_progress, resolved or dismissed on one ledger row; the next ledger read shows it.
[`talonic_contract_check_settings`](/docs/mcp/tools/contract-check-settings): The settings with what is needed to choose them: data products, the CRM table's columns, sample rows, contract types.
[`talonic_contract_check_save_settings`](/docs/mcp/tools/contract-check-save-settings): Save which data product the contracts come from and the check settings.
[`talonic_contract_check_column_values`](/docs/mcp/tools/contract-check-column-values): Up to 100 distinct values of one CRM column, to choose a setting from; more: true when there are more.
[`talonic_chart_pdfs_page`](/docs/mcp/tools/chart-pdfs-page): One window of the workspace's PDF documents with total.
[`talonic_chart_read_charts_available`](/docs/mcp/tools/chart-read-charts-available): { available }: whether reading the charts of selected documents is offered here.
[`talonic_chart_read_charts_preview`](/docs/mcp/tools/chart-read-charts-preview): What reading the charts of these documents would read and cost at most.
[`talonic_chart_read_charts`](/docs/mcp/tools/chart-read-charts): Read the charts of the selected documents, one outcome per document.

content.text: Keep each company's documents apart with accounts, and check balance, pricing and what credits went on.

items: [`talonic_get_balance`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-balance): Read the workspace's Talonic credit balance, EUR value, tier, 30-day burn, and projected runway.
[`talonic_get_pricing`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-pricing): Read Talonic's machine-readable credit pricing catalog: fixed per-unit rates so you can predict spend BEFORE running anything.
[`talonic_get_usage`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-usage): Read the workspace's per-function credit consumption over a trailing window: where the credits actually went.
[`talonic_list_accounts`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-accounts): List the workspace's accounts: the companies (portfolio companies, clients, entities) whose documents it keeps apart.
[`talonic_create_account`](/docs/mcp/tools/create-account): Create an account: a company whose documents the workspace keeps apart, so answers about it never mix in another company's files.
[`talonic_workspace_billing`](/docs/mcp/tools/workspace-billing): Plan, credit balance, auto-reload settings, whether the workspace may buy credits directly, and the credit packs.
[`talonic_workspace_buy_credits_link`](/docs/mcp/tools/workspace-buy-credits-link): A URL a person opens to buy prepaid credits.
[`talonic_workspace_billing_portal_link`](/docs/mcp/tools/workspace-billing-portal-link): A one-time URL a person opens to manage payment methods and download invoices.

[`talonic_workspace_create_support_ticket`](/docs/mcp/tools/workspace-create-support-ticket): Sends a request to Talonic support with your name, e-mail and workspace, and returns its reference to quote in follow-ups.
[`talonic_workspace_deletion_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/workspace-deletion-status): Whether this workspace is scheduled for deletion, and when.
[`talonic_workspace_cancel_deletion`](/docs/mcp/tools/workspace-cancel-deletion): Cancels a deletion this workspace scheduled and restores its previous access.

content.text: Approve, invite and change access for team members (a change is proposed, then confirmed), and keep retention policies, legal holds, the audit log and erasure requests in order.

items: [`talonic_team_list_members`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-list-members): Every member of the workspace with role and status (and permissions, when you may manage the team).
[`talonic_team_list_pending`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-list-pending): People who asked to join the workspace and wait for approval.
[`talonic_team_approve_member`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-approve-member): Admits one person who asked to join.
[`talonic_team_reject_member`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-reject-member): Declines one request to join the workspace.
[`talonic_team_invite_member`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-invite-member): Invites a person by e-mail with a role.
[`talonic_team_preview_access`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-preview-access): What one member holds right now: role, permissions, custom role and groups.
[`talonic_team_list_roles`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-list-roles): The roles this workspace defined itself, each with its base role and permissions.
[`talonic_team_list_groups`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-list-groups): The workspace's groups of members.
[`talonic_team_propose_access_change`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-propose-access-change): Shows exactly what a change would change (before and after) and stores it as a proposal.
[`talonic_team_confirm_access_change`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-confirm-access-change): Makes a proposed access change after checking it again against the current state and your permissions.
[`talonic_team_cancel_access_change`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-cancel-access-change): Cancels one of your access proposals; nothing changes.
[`talonic_team_access_activity`](/docs/mcp/tools/team-access-activity): The latest access changes, confirmations and refusals recorded in this workspace.
[`talonic_records_list_retention_policies`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-list-retention-policies): The workspace's retention policies: how long documents are kept and what happens when that time ends.
[`talonic_records_create_retention_policy`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-create-retention-policy): Creates a retention policy.
[`talonic_records_list_dispositions`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-list-dispositions): Documents whose retention ended and that wait for a person's decision.
[`talonic_records_list_legal_holds`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-list-legal-holds): Legal holds and what they cover.
[`talonic_records_create_legal_hold`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-create-legal-hold): Places a legal hold on the whole workspace, one source, or a set of documents.
[`talonic_records_add_hold_documents`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-add-hold-documents): Adds documents to a document-set legal hold.
[`talonic_records_list_audit_events`](/docs/mcp/tools/records-list-audit-events): Reads the tamper-evident audit log.

faq.question: Why does my agent not list some of these tools?

faq.question: What does talonic_search do?
faq.answer: It finds documents, fields, schemas and sources whose name or text contains your keyword, and returns their ids. Search with one short, singular word or an exact file name.

faq.answer: Use search to find a document or field by name ('Acme', 'invoice'). Use filter for conditions on extracted values ('invoices over 1000 EUR').

title: talonic_filter
seoTitle: talonic_filter — Filter Documents by Extracted Fields
description: MCP tool that finds documents by their extracted field values with conditions such as eq, gt, between and contains, and reports fields it couldn't match.

content.text: Find documents by their extracted field VALUES using composable conditions (e.g. 'invoices where total > 1000').

items: **Use it when:** value-based criteria on extracted fields — numeric/date/text comparisons or presence checks.
**Not for:** free-text / concept search (use talonic_search) · a single document by id (use talonic_get_document).

**Arguments:** conditions[] (AND-ed). Each = EXACTLY ONE of `field` (canonical name) or `field_id` (UUID), an `operator`, and usually a `value`. Operators: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between (needs `value` AND `value_to`), contains, is_empty / is_not_empty (no value). `value`/`value_to` are string|number|boolean matching the field type (ISO YYYY-MM-DD for dates).

**Text filters:** for eq/contains/is_not_empty on a text field, just TRY a natural field name ('currency', 'vendor_name') — names resolve server-side and an unresolved field surfaces in warnings[] rather than erroring. Do NOT block on discovering the field first; search-first is only required for numeric operators.

**Numeric guard:** gt/gte/lt/lte/between only work when the field's dataType is 'number'. Call talonic_search first and check dataType; a numeric op on a string field returns zero matches. If the response has `warnings[]`, surface them to the user — do not silently retry.
**Returns:** data[] (matching documents with field values), total, warnings[].

content.text: Listed in every Talonic MCP session, local or hosted.

items: **Reads only.** It never changes workspace data.
**Cost:** no credits.

faq.question: How do I filter documents by field value?
faq.answer: Use talonic_filter with field names and operators such as eq, gt, between or contains. Field names are matched for you; one it can't match comes back in warnings[].

faq.question: How do I find the correct canonical field names for filtering?
faq.answer: For text fields, try the natural name ('vendor_name', 'currency'). For numbers and dates, call talonic_search first: the canonical names are in fields[].canonicalName.

faq.question: Can I combine free-text search with field filters?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass `search` alongside `conditions` to combine a keyword with value conditions in one call.

faq.question: What operators are available for talonic_filter?
faq.answer: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between (with value_to), contains, is_empty and is_not_empty. The number comparisons work only on fields stored as numbers.

faq.question: Why does my filter return zero results even though matching documents exist?
faq.answer: Usually a number comparison on a field stored as text, for example amounts with currency symbols. Check the field's dataType first, and read warnings[] on the response.

faq.question: Does talonic_get_pricing require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The pricing catalog is public, so an agent can read rates before signing up or provisioning a key. Call it with no arguments; it is read-only and safe to call at any time.

faq.question: How does an agent compute the cost of a job from the catalog?
faq.answer: Multiply the credits per unit by the number of units (pages, fields or operations), apply the multiplier (batch work costs half), and divide by credits_per_eur for euros.

faq.question: Which operations are free in the catalog?
faq.answer: The catalog marks free units with `free: true`. Searching, listing, look-ups and reading stored text are free; reading new documents, filling fields and matching use credits.

**Not for:** the remaining balance (use talonic_get_balance) or per-unit rates (use talonic_get_pricing).
**Arguments:** days (optional, default 30, clamped 1-365).
**Returns:** period_days, total_credits, and by_function[] — each { operation_type, operations, credits }, highest spend first.

**Cost:** no credits.

params.description: Trailing window in days (default 30). Range: 1 to 365.

faq.question: How is talonic_get_usage different from talonic_get_balance?
faq.answer: Balance says what is left (and how long it lasts); usage says what was spent and on what. Use balance to check headroom and usage to see where credits went.

faq.question: What window does talonic_get_usage cover?
faq.answer: The last 30 days by default. Pass days to change it, anywhere from 1 to 365. The response echoes period_days so the agent can confirm the window it summarized.

faq.question: Why is the breakdown empty?
faq.answer: Rows appear once work has been charged in the window. A new workspace, or one with no charged work in the period, returns an empty breakdown; widen `days` to look further back.

title: talonic_request_upload
seoTitle: talonic_request_upload — Upload Links for Large Files
description: MCP tool that gives the user a browser link to upload a file too large for a chat tool call. Returns the link, a reserved document_id and when the link expires.

**Arguments:** filename (with extension); optional account (company name or id from talonic_list_accounts) so the file stays with that company; optional add_to_workspace (true = process it fully into workspace data for later questions and SQL; default false = text only, for a following talonic_extract).

**Returns:** upload_url, document_id, expires_at. After the user uploads, poll talonic_get_document on that document_id until status is 'completed' (or 'extracted' when add_to_workspace is false), then call talonic_extract if you need fields. If status becomes ocr_failed, extraction_failed, or error, stop polling and report the failure to the user.

items: **Not read-only.** It can add to or change workspace data.
**Cost:** The link is free; reading the uploaded file uses credits.

faq.question: When should the agent use `talonic_request_upload` instead of `file_data`?
faq.answer: In Claude.ai and ChatGPT, where a tool call can carry only about 32 KB; real documents are larger and arrive cut short as file_data. Local installs (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Continue, Cowork) can pass files by path instead.

faq.question: Does a user message like 'uploaded' mean the file is ready to extract?
faq.answer: No. It means the browser finished sending the file; Talonic still needs a short while to read it. Check talonic_get_document until status is 'completed' before extracting.

faq.question: What happens if the user never opens the upload link?
faq.answer: The reserved document stays in pending_upload. The link stops working at expires_at; ask for a new one with talonic_request_upload, which reserves a new document_id.

faq.question: Can the agent PUT the file to the upload_url itself?
faq.answer: Usually not: hosted chat clients can't send data to arbitrary addresses. And the user should choose the file anyway, so give them the link.

faq.question: How do I keep a company's files together, and make them workspace data?
faq.answer: Pass `account` (a company name, alias or id from talonic_list_accounts; create one with talonic_create_account) so the document belongs to that company, and `add_to_workspace: true` so it is fully processed and can be asked about later. Without add_to_workspace only its text is kept, for one talonic_extract call.

faq.question: Why a separate tool instead of changing `talonic_extract`?
faq.answer: Keeping the upload step separate means the user sees the link and knows what is happening, and talonic_extract behaves the same for every file.

faq.question: What is an execution epoch?
faq.answer: A number that identifies your claim. Every claim or reclaim gets a new one, and calls with an old one are refused, so an agent whose claim ran out cannot overwrite a newer result.

faq.question: Can I claim a task that is already claimed?
faq.answer: Only once its lease has expired. A live claim by another actor returns HTTP 409; after lease_expires_at passes without a heartbeat, the same claim call succeeds as a reclaim and increments the execution epoch.

faq.question: What happens if I claim a task and never finish it?
faq.answer: Nothing is written. The lease runs out and the task can be claimed again; if timeout_at passes with no submission, the task's timeout_fallthrough (hold, skip or route_to_review) decides what happens to the document. An abandoned claim never damages data; it only delays the document.

faq.question: How often should an agent heartbeat?
faq.answer: Only when needed, comfortably before lease_expires_at. Use the updated lease expiry returned by each successful heartbeat rather than a fixed client-side assumption.

faq.question: What does a heartbeat return?
faq.answer: The task's metadata with the new lease_expires_at and the current execution_epoch. Never the input; the claim already gave you that.

faq.question: My heartbeat returned HTTP 409 — can I still submit?
faq.answer: No. A 409 means your execution epoch is stale: the lease expired and the task was reclaimed or withdrawn. Submits with that epoch will also be rejected, so discard the in-flight work and claim a different task.

faq.question: How is a decision task different from an Agent task?
faq.answer: An agent task asks for output fields for one document in a Spec. A decision task asks for one app run's decision: it must match the app's output contract, cite evidence from the task's input, and is recorded as decided by an external agent. Both use the same claim, lease, heartbeat and execution-epoch rules.

faq.question: Why does the tool return 403 insufficient_scope, or carry talonic/can_invoke: false in its _meta?
faq.answer: Deciding is a separate permission. A tlnc_ key needs a decide grant on that app from a workspace owner. A connector session needs the apps:decide scope and a role of senior member or above, checked on every call. A connector added before that scope existed lacks it: the tools are listed but marked not callable, and removing and re-adding the Talonic connector fixes it.

faq.question: What do the decision task statuses mean?
faq.answer: available means no one holds the task; claimed means an agent holds a live lease; submitted means a decision was accepted and the run resumed; released means the claimant gave it back (it returns to available); failed means the claimant declared it undecidable and the fallback applied; timed_out means the SLA passed; cancelled means the run was cancelled or the task withdrawn.

faq.question: Why does reading the package return HTTP 409?

faq.question: How often should an agent heartbeat a decision task?
faq.answer: Comfortably inside the lease: with the default 120-second lease, roughly every 60 seconds while the decision is still being worked on. Stop once the task is submitted, released or failed.

faq.question: Can a heartbeat extend past the SLA deadline?
faq.answer: No. The lease is clamped to sla_deadline_at. If the decision cannot be made before then, submit what you have with an honest confidence, release the task, or fail it with a reason so the fallback policy runs deliberately rather than by timeout.

title: talonic_submit_decision_task

Rejections are HTTP 422 with the reason and change nothing; the task stays claimed under your epoch, so fix and resubmit before the lease ends.
**Not for:** giving the task back undecided (talonic_release_decision_task) or declaring it undecidable (talonic_fail_decision_task). Stale epoch is HTTP 409.

faq.answer: Only a db: or ref: locator naming a connection or reference table the app is allowed to read; those are accepted and recorded. Any other locator from outside the input, and the reserved api: prefix, is refused.

title: talonic_integrations_connect
seoTitle: talonic_integrations_connect — Connect Through the Browser
description: MCP tool that starts connecting Gmail, Google Drive, SharePoint and other accounts: it returns a link the person opens to sign in at the provider and finish.

content.text: Start connecting an account through a browser sign-in. Returns `authorize_url`, `id` (the authorization id) and `expires_at` (30 minutes). Give the user the link: they must open it in a browser while signed in to Talonic, in this workspace, as the same person this connection acts for, then confirm and finish the provider's sign-in. Nothing is connected until they do. Then call talonic_integrations_connect_status with the id until status is connected, failed, expired or cancelled. Only for connectors whose method is authorize (talonic_integrations_connectors). Optional: `send` (gmail, outlook: the mailbox may also send mail), `intake` (gmail, notion, slack: what to read first). Connecting the same account again renews the existing connection. Personal connections (mailboxes, notes, a person's own drive) show their content only as the connecting person's access allows; other people in the workspace may see the connection without its content. Errors: 503 connector_not_configured (not offered on this deployment), 403 with a reason (missing consent or permission). NOT FOR S3, Azure Blob, SQL, Kendox, Granola or upload links: they need credentials, which never pass through an agent conversation.

Listed when the session can read the workspace's sources (`sources:read` on a connector session); connecting, importing and sync settings need `sources:write`. Being listed only means the tool is visible: Talonic checks your role again on every call.

title: Files and uploads from an agent
seoTitle: Files and Uploads from an AI Agent: Talonic MCP — Talonic
description: Four ways an agent gets a file to Talonic: a document already in the workspace, a public URL, a local path or bytes, or an upload link the user opens.

content.text: Before Talonic can read a document, the file has to reach it. This page shows the four ways an agent can do that, which one to use, and what to tell the user while a file is on its way.

items: **Already in the workspace.** Use its `document_id`. If the user names the file, find the id with [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) (search by file name or one keyword). Free and instant.
**On a public URL.** Pass `file_url` (https). Talonic fetches it. Good for links the user pastes.
**On the user's machine, in a local install.** Pass `file_path`; the local server reads the file. Small files can also go as `file_data` (base64) with `filename`.
**Anything else, especially in Claude.ai or ChatGPT.** Call [`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload) and give the user the link. They open it in their browser and drop the file.

content.text: Hosted chat clients cap the size of a tool call (around 32 KB), which is smaller than most real documents. A file sent as `file_data` there arrives cut short and comes back with empty fields. Use an upload link instead.
The upload link, step by step

items: The agent calls [`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload) with the `filename`. Pass `account` to file it under one company, and `add_to_workspace: true` if the user will ask questions about it later (otherwise only its text is kept for the next extraction).
It returns `upload_url`, a `document_id` reserved for the file, and `expires_at`. The agent shows the user the link and says when it expires.
The user opens the link and drops the file. The agent checks [`talonic_get_document`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-document) every few seconds.
When `status` is `completed` (or `extracted` without `add_to_workspace`), the file is ready: extract fields, read its text, or ask about it.

content.title: Status while a file is on its way

params.name: pending_upload
params.description: Link issued; the user has not dropped the file yet.

params.name: uploading
params.description: The file is arriving. Keep checking.

params.name: ocr_failed / extraction_failed / error
params.description: Stop checking and tell the user; the file could not be read. A clearer scan or the original file usually works.

content.text: PDFs (text or scanned), images and phone photos, Word documents (DOCX) and emails. Long documents take longer; very large files are better sent as an upload link or a URL than as bytes.

If the workspace holds documents for several companies (clients, portfolio companies, entities), pass `account` when uploading. Questions scoped to that account never mix in another company's files. [`talonic_list_accounts`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-accounts) lists them; [`talonic_create_account`](/docs/mcp/tools/create-account) adds one.
Issuing a link and checking status are free. Reading a new file uses credits, as in the web app; [`talonic_get_pricing`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-pricing) shows the rates.

faq.question: Why does my agent ask me to open a link instead of reading the file I attached?
faq.answer: Hosted chat clients limit how much data one tool call can carry, so an attached document would arrive incomplete. The upload link sends the whole file straight from your browser to your workspace.

faq.question: How long is an upload link valid?
faq.answer: Until the `expires_at` time returned with it. If it expires, ask the agent for a new link; nothing is lost.
